newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit recovers,slides back on sustained pressure.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers,slides back on sustained pressure.

text.p: The ringgit recovered from its morning lows, but eased back below 2.65 a dollar in the afternoon on sustained overseas selling, dealers said.
They said the slide was triggered by a renewed speculative attack in the morning on the Singapore dollar and Thai baht.
"The trend is very strong. The dollar is very strong, with dollar/mark above 1.83. It is a sentiment thing," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
He said there was a mild reaction late morning to comments by Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, who lashed out against currency speculators calling them "rogues".
"The PM did not say anything that showed there would be concrete steps taken against speculators," the dealer said.
Mahathir told reporters the Association of South East Asian Nations, whose members' currencies are under attack, could form a common law to curb speculation.
Dealers said volumes continue to be thin and a large part of the ringgit selling was made up by non-speculative players.
"Today genuine investors, corporates and even manufacturers were hedging their positions because they are scared of the ringgit falling further," said an analyst in Singapore.
At 0945 GMT, ringgit was at 2.6495/6525 to a dollar. It hit 2.6500/50 in the morning.
